title: Congruence of finite exact-derived pasting expressions
statement: Let $I$ be any indexing type and let $C_i$ be abelian categories with chosen ordinary unbounded derived categories. Use exact-functor words, their ordinary and derived interpretations, and finite transformation expressions as in [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting]. For words $P,R$ with the same endpoints and expressions $e,f:P\Rightarrow R$, if $e$ and $f$ have equal ordinary interpretations, their derived interpretations are equal. There is no finiteness assumption on $I$: the words and expressions themselves are finite.

source.place: Tags 015F and 04VG; natural-transformation localization and finite expression factorization

proof.text: Restrict the two derived transformations along the quasi-isomorphism localization Q. For each complex K, expression_factors identifies each restricted component followed by the target word comparison with the source word comparison followed by Q of the ordinary complex component.

The assumed equality of ordinary expressions gives equality of the right sides. Cancel the invertible target comparison. The natural-transformation restriction functor along Q is fully faithful, so the derived transformations agree. Only the individual expression trees are finite; no finiteness of the entire indexing type is used. Private component lemmas implement whiskering, compositor and associator evaluations and the vertical, horizontal and cube pasting trees used by the parent.

proof_origin.place: E8: reuse of the existing expression_factors proof; explicit finite expression trees and termwise component calculations.
